stem:
The diagram shows parallel lines $m$ and $n$ cut by transversal $t$. One same-side interior angle is marked $70^{\circ}$.

Which claim correctly gives the other same-side interior angle?

options.text: The other same-side interior angle is $110^{\circ}$, because same-side interior angles on parallel lines add to $180^{\circ}$.
The other same-side interior angle is $70^{\circ}$, because same-side interior angles on parallel lines are equal.
The other same-side interior angle is $20^{\circ}$, from $90^{\circ}-70^{\circ}$.
The other same-side interior angle is $140^{\circ}$, from doubling $70^{\circ}$.

teacher.key_rationale: Same-side interior angles on a transversal of parallel lines are supplementary, so 180-70=110. They are not equal. Subtracting from 90 or doubling 70 uses the wrong relation.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle figure as two parallel lines with a transversal and same-side interior marks 70° and x.
